evidence.prompt_and_options:
7. A cyclist applies a rim brake. Which interaction directly provides the intended frictional braking torque on the wheel?
A. Air resistance on the rider
B. Chain tension driving the rear wheel
C. Normal support from the level road
D. Brake pad rubbing on the wheel rim
evidence.key_and_feedback: 7. Key D. A: This retards the bicycle but is not the intended pad-on-wheel braking torque. B: Driving tension supplies a driving torque rather than the stated brake interaction. C: This support is perpendicular to the road, not the pad’s tangential friction force. D: The pad’s tangential friction force on the rim produces the braking moment.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
2. Compared with an ordinary nonmetal, which additional mobile particles help transfer thermal energy through a metal?
A. Ions flowing through the metal
B. Whole atoms flowing from hot to cold
C. Mobile electrons
D. Neutrons migrating between nuclei
evidence.key_and_feedback: 2. Key C. A: Metal ions mainly vibrate near fixed positions; they do not flow through the solid. B: Bulk material flow is not ordinary conduction through the solid. C: They transfer energy through the metal. D: Neutrons are bound within nuclei and are not the mobile thermal carriers here.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
3. Which sample can sustain ordinary bulk convection within it?
A. An evacuated vessel
B. Liquid water
C. A rigid copper block
D. A solid rubber block
evidence.key_and_feedback: 3. Key B. A: A vacuum has no fluid to circulate. B: Its material can circulate, carrying thermal energy. C: A solid block does not circulate bodily inside itself. D: Solid material cannot form the ordinary circulating fluid current.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
3. Which band is named for satellite telephone links in this course?
A. Low-frequency broadcast radio
B. Microwaves
C. Visible light
D. Infrared
evidence.key_and_feedback: 3. Key B. A: This option is outside the microwave frequency band named for the satellite-link example. B: They can carry the communication signal. C: Not the named satellite-link band here. D: Not the named satellite-link band here.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
8. An initially neutral material gains electrons and no other charge is transferred. What is its resulting net charge?
A. It depends only on the rod mass
B. Positive
C. Negative
D. Neutral regardless of the gain
evidence.key_and_feedback: 8. Key C. A: Charge balance depends on electrons and protons, not mass alone. B: Gaining negative electrons makes net charge more negative. C: Electrons add negative charge. D: A net added electron imbalance changes charge.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
11. An initially neutral conductor on an insulating stand is earthed while a negative rod is held nearby. Which sequence leaves the conductor positively charged?
A. Disconnect Earth before bringing the rod nearby
B. Remove the rod, then disconnect Earth
C. Remove the rod and keep Earth connected
D. Disconnect Earth, then remove the rod
evidence.key_and_feedback: 11. Key D. A: Without an earth path while the rod is present, electrons cannot leave to create the intended net positive charge. B: Electrons can return through the earth path before it is removed. C: The remaining earth path permits neutralisation. D: The rod is still repelling electrons when the earth path is removed, so an electron deficit remains.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
12. A 440 W training appliance operates at 220 V. For this steady-load exercise choose the smallest listed fuse rating above its normal current: 1 A, 3 A, 10 A or 13 A.
A. 13 A
B. 3 A
C. 1 A
D. 10 A
evidence.key_and_feedback: 12. Key B. A: It is not the smallest suitable given option. B: Normal current is 440/220 = 2 A; 3 A is the smallest listed rating above 2 A. C: It is below normal current. D: A smaller suitable option is given.

evidence.prompt_and_options:
10. With positive plate above and negative below, which way does beta-minus deflect?
A. Downward
B. Toward whichever plate is closer regardless of charge
C. Upward
D. Straight through with no deflection
evidence.key_and_feedback: 10. Key C. A: This is the positive-particle direction, not negative beta. B: Distance to a plate does not set the force direction: beta-minus has negative charge and is attracted toward the upper positive plate. C: The negative particle force opposes the downward field. D: Beta-minus has charge and experiences an electric force.

evidence.prompt: State Newton’s first law, including the force condition.
evidence.answer: With zero resultant force, an object stays at rest or continues moving at the same velocity.
rubric: 1 mark for both the zero-resultant condition and unchanged velocity/rest. Accept no acceleration when forces balance; do not require zero individual forces.
Accept an equivalent scientific name, property, unit or fact answering the requested feature; do not award unrelated facts.

evidence.prompt: State what friction opposes between two touching surfaces.
evidence.answer: Friction opposes their relative sliding or tendency to slide.
rubric: 1 mark: opposes relative motion or impending slip at the contact. Accept grip preventing sliding. Do not credit a claim that friction always opposes the object’s velocity.
Accept an equivalent scientific name, property, unit or fact answering the requested feature; do not award unrelated facts.

evidence.prompt: State any two energy forms or stores and give one example of each.
evidence.answer: Examples include kinetic energy of a moving trolley, gravitational potential energy of raised water, strain energy of a stretched spring, chemical energy in fuel, nuclear energy in a fuel nucleus and internal energy in warm water.
rubric: Any two distinct correct form–example pairs, 1 mark each. Accept elastic for strain, thermal for internal, light/radiant energy from a lamp, sound energy from a vibrating source, or electrical energy in an appropriate transfer example. No second mark for two examples of the same form.
Accept an equivalent scientific name, property, unit or fact answering the requested feature; do not award unrelated facts.

evidence.prompt: Explain how a crowbar can lift a load with a smaller effort.
evidence.answer: The support is its fulcrum and the effort acts farther from it than the load. The longer perpendicular effort arm gives the needed turning moment with less force, while the effort travels farther.
rubric: 1 mark for identifying a longer effort arm relative to the load arm.
1 mark for the resulting smaller force at equal moment, with greater effort travel. Accept another named lever with the same correctly located pivot, load and effort.
Credit a linked physical process and its effect; a cause named without the requested consequence is incomplete.

evidence.prompt: State one named use of gears.
evidence.answer: Bicycle gears change the relationship between pedalling speed and wheel turning effect.
rubric: Any one named use for 1 mark: bicycle gearing, car gearbox, clock or hand drill, with a relevant transmission/speed/turning-effect role. A machine name without any gear function is insufficient.
Accept an equivalent scientific name, property, unit or fact answering the requested feature; do not award unrelated facts.

evidence.prompt: Explain how a crane’s ideal two-section movable pulley reduces the lifting effort.
evidence.answer: Two rope sections support the load, each carrying the same tension. The effort is half the load force, while twice the rope length must be pulled for a given rise.
rubric: 1 mark for two supporting tensions sharing the load.
1 mark for effort half the load with twice the rope travel. Accept a correctly labelled equivalent pulley diagram; do not apply this force reduction to one fixed pulley.
Credit a linked physical process and its effect; a cause named without the requested consequence is incomplete.

evidence.prompt: Explain the corresponding functions of iris/aperture and retina/film in an eye and camera.
evidence.answer: The iris varies the pupil opening as a camera aperture controls the light entering. The retina receives the eye’s image as film or a sensor receives the camera’s real inverted image.
rubric: 1 mark for iris/pupil opening compared with adjustable aperture as a light-admission control. Accept diaphragm as the camera part.
1 mark for retina compared with film or sensor as the image-receiving light-sensitive surface. Do not credit the lens as the receiving surface.
Credit the contrast on the same basis for both cases; repeating one side does not establish the difference.

evidence.prompt: State how illumination creates the charge pattern on a photocopier drum.
evidence.answer: Light discharges the exposed regions of the charged drum; unlit image regions retain charge and attract toner.
rubric: 1 mark for light discharging the exposed drum regions so the unlit image retains charge. Accept illuminated areas lose their charge. Toner attraction without the light-discharge stage is insufficient for this prompt.
Accept an equivalent scientific name, property, unit or fact answering the requested feature; do not award unrelated facts.

evidence.prompt: Explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
evidence.answer: Solids, liquids and gases contain particles that can pass on sound vibrations. A vacuum has no material particles to transmit this mechanical wave.
rubric: Credit 1 (1): Sound needs particle interactions in solids/liquids/gases.
Credit 2 (1): Vacuum lacks them; sound in liquids is not forbidden.

Maximum 2 marks. Accept equivalent scientifically correct wording or a labelled representation of the same points. Count each distinct idea once; an unsupported keyword alone is not a causal explanation.
Accepted alternative wording: “region with no material particles” for “vacuum”. The stated directions, quantities and conditions are still required.
Credit a linked physical process and its effect; a cause named without the requested consequence is incomplete.
